prompt: I'm retiring in 8 weeks. My 401k has $620,000 total — $240,000 of that is company stock I've accumulated over 25 years at work. My HR told me the average cost basis on those shares is about $38,000. My financial advisor says to roll everything to a Vanguard IRA for simplicity, better fund options, and lower fees. Should I just do the full rollover?
assertions: Claude explicitly flags NUA (Net Unrealized Appreciation) as a strategy that must be evaluated before rolling company stock to an IRA
Claude explains the key tax consequence: rolling company stock to an IRA permanently converts the unrealized appreciation from LTCG rates to ordinary income rates on future withdrawals
Claude explains the NUA mechanics: take a lump-sum distribution of company shares in-kind, pay ordinary income tax on cost basis ($38k) now, sell shares later at LTCG rates on the $202k appreciation
Claude explicitly states that NUA treatment is irreversible — once you roll to an IRA, you permanently lose the ability to use NUA treatment on those shares
Claude does NOT simply validate 'roll everything to Vanguard for simplicity' without at minimum flagging NUA as an irreversible opportunity requiring evaluation before the rollover
